title: Académies rely on intérimaires as thousands of teaching posts stay unfilled
content: More than 4,100 teaching posts remain unfilled six weeks after the *rentrée*, and the académies have responded by expanding the use of *intérimaires*, according to figures compiled by the rectorats and confirmed by the Ministère de l’Éducation nationale.

The shortage is concentrated in mathematics, the sciences and the lycées professionnels, where the gap between the number of posts and the number of qualified candidates has widened for the fourth consecutive year. In six académies, including Vallonne and Marbre, the requirement for a completed concours has been waived for intérim contracts of up to one school year.
img::/gazette/images/7/interimaires-protest.webp::« Stop the chaos — hire permanent professeurs » : le cortège devant l’académie de Vallonne. Photographie : Presses de Vallonne.

“We are not filling posts any more; we are preventing classes from collapsing,” said a rectoral official who asked not to be named. The same official confirmed that several intérimaires are assigned to subjects outside their original training, and that inspecteurs have been asked to monitor the most fragile situations.

A collectif de parents in Vallonne published an open letter on Tuesday describing “a permanent improvisation” in the second year of the lycée, where mathematics has been taught by three different teachers since September. The collectif has requested a meeting with the rectorat before the autumn holidays.

The Syndicat des enseignants des lycées called the figures a predictable consequence of a recruitment system that draws fewer candidates each year, and repeated its demand for an emergency second session of the concours in January and a revision of starting salaries.

The ministry points to a recruitment campaign launched in September and to a reform of initial teacher training planned for 2027. Officials acknowledge that the *intérim* system, originally designed as a short-term measure, has become a structural component of staffing in the eastern republics.

Consultants who advise académies on staffing warn that the quality of instruction is not the only concern: intérimaires leave at twice the rate of tenured teachers, and each departure restarts the recruitment cycle. The ministry declined to provide figures on departures before the end of the calendar year.
author: Texte : Gaël Fontaine, correspondant éducation — Presses de Vallonne · Photographies : Rémi Chastel — Agence Continentale
